clue.text: Support regular feature in newspaper

blocks.note: first meaning: an upright pillar holding up a structure
second meaning: a recurring article by the same writer

explanation.surface: Someone backing a favourite weekly slot in their paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an architectural pillar bearing weight and a regular piece written for a periodical.

clue.text: I sing about top Italian wine from Tuscany

indicators.note: about means going around, so the singing word wraps the single letter that precedes it
the top of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Italian is kept

blocks.note: to chant is to sing in a monotone
taken as written
first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: A singer around a famous Italian wine region, praising the local red.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes inside the singing word, after its first two letters, and the opening of Italian is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is the classic red produced in the hills of central Italy around Florence and Siena.

clue.text: Lawful years back in the Fifties

indicators.note: going back means the word for years is read from right to left
in places the turned word inside the letters standing for the Fifties

blocks.note: an age is a long span of years
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: Something permitted again, as it was back in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fifties are not a decade here but two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lawful is permitted by the law, which is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Repair man takes a stroll

indicators.note: takes means receives into itself, so the repairer holds the single letter

blocks.note: a mender is someone who repairs things
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handyman going out for a gentle walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander slowly and aimlessly, like a winding river, much as a leisurely walker does.

clue.text: A political party is hard work

blocks.note: first meaning: the main British party of the left
second meaning: strenuous physical toil

explanation.surface: A grumble that being in politics is exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of the two big UK parties, alongside the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the name of the British party founded by trade unions and an ordinary noun for toil.

clue.text: Given a note, hand around for hound

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about and set in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
F is one of the musical notes
as printed this does not work; the clue almost certainly misprints hang, whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone handed a banknote, passing it round to pay for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed hand seems to be a misprint for hang: only hang supplies the letters needed after A and F.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afghan is a tall long-haired breed of sighthound originally from the mountains of Afghanistan.

clue.text: Agreed on a different drink

indicators.note: different tells us the letters take a changed arrangement

blocks.note: all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: People who finally agreed to switch to another beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with citrus fruit juice.

clue.text: People are always breaking these discs

blocks.note: first meaning: best-ever performances, which athletes keep beating
second meaning: vinyl albums for playing music

explanation.surface: Clumsy people forever smashing their vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking suggests snapping brittle vinyl, but the first sense is beating a best performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both best-ever achievements in sport and gramophone discs carrying recorded music.

clue.text: In which you might write "ballcock is apt to go wrong"

indicators.note: going wrong means falling out of proper order, so the quoted letters are jumbled

blocks.note: every letter of the quoted words

explanation.surface: An instruction about how to write out a plumber's warning about a toilet cistern valve.
explanation.walkthrough: A ballcock is the floating valve in a cistern. The quotation marks make it look like text to be written; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters printed separately are the style forms ask you to fill in, so you might write anything in them.

clue.text: It's right for a Tory

blocks.note: surface reading: something correct or proper for a Conservative
setter's reading: right names a political side, the faction where Tories sit

explanation.walkthrough: Right looks like correct, but it is the right of the political spectrum; Tories are British Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A party faction is called by this term, and a Conservative belongs to the right one.

clue.text: E.g. in a union it shows loyalty

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a union

blocks.note: the abbreviation for for example, taken as written
an alliance is a union of parties or nations

explanation.surface: A trade union demonstrating the solidarity of its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithful commitment owed to a ruler, nation or cause, the same as fidelity.

clue.text: Out of clothes?

blocks.note: surface reading: a shop that has sold all its garments
setter's reading: a person who is out of their garments, that is naked

explanation.definitionFit: Clad means dressed, so the negated form describes someone wearing nothing at all.

clue.text: Warhorses are often attached to batteries

blocks.note: first meaning: horses ridden into battle by cavalry
second meaning: devices plugged in to replenish electric power

explanation.surface: Cavalry mounts assigned to artillery units.
explanation.walkthrough: Batteries suggests guns, fitting the warhorses, but the second sense is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both mounts ridden into combat and units that restore power to rechargeable cells.

clue.text: Untidy crew I sack for flippant remark

indicators.note: untidy suggests things left in a disorderly jumble, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of these three words

explanation.surface: A captain firing a slovenly crew in exchange for some cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, joking quip, the kind of glib comment a cheeky person makes.

clue.text: Rearranged medical after former wife cried out

indicators.note: rearranged plainly asks for the letters to be put in a new order
after says the reworked piece comes behind the other, so the former spouse goes first

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone shouting when a health check was reorganised after their divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to shout suddenly, so the past tense matches having called out loudly.

clue.text: Gathering for a church service

blocks.note: first meaning: a large body or crowd
second meaning: the Catholic Eucharist rite

explanation.surface: A congregation assembling for worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large crowd of people and the central Catholic Eucharistic liturgy.

clue.text: Cossack dropping lettuce into container

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of something, so part of the dancer's word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
cos is a variety of lettuce, also called romaine

explanation.surface: A Russian horseman dropping salad leaves into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the lettuce variety from the front of Cossack leaves the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack is a large bag of coarse cloth used for holding and carrying goods.

clue.text: Female singer, so quiet musically, ran round

blocks.note: taken as written
p for piano is the musical marking for soft
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A singer who performed softly and then went off for a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano has the highest singing voice, usually belonging to a woman.

clue.text: Long to eat Italian food?

blocks.note: surface reading: craving a meal at an Italian restaurant
setter's reading: long is an adjective describing the length of a pasta strand that is eaten

explanation.walkthrough: Long reads as a verb meaning yearn, but it describes the shape of the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta comes in long thin strings, a staple dish of Italian cooking eaten twirled on a fork.

clue.text: Rubbish bin's first put in car servicing centre

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the bin word
put in says that letter is placed inside the servicing place

blocks.note: opening letter of bin
a garage repairs and services cars

explanation.surface: A rubbish bin dumped at the local car repair shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is household waste, the American word for refuse thrown away.

clue.text: Schoolmaster found in class trying to beat each erring schoolboy

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the following run of words

blocks.note: surface padding that sets the classroom scene
running across these three words
surface padding completing the picture of a caning

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned classroom where a master canes a misbehaving boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a man who instructs pupils, which is what this job title covers.

clue.text: Game supervised by a high court judge?

definitions.text: Game supervised by a high court judge?

blocks.clueFragment: Game supervised by a high court judge
blocks.note: surface reading: some contest overseen by a senior member of the judiciary
setter's reading: an official seated high above a sports court, the umpire in his raised chair

explanation.walkthrough: A High Court judge sits in Britain's senior civil court; here the court is a sports surface and the judge sits high on a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: This racket sport is played on a court and officiated by an umpire perched in a tall chair.

clue.text: Obvious if father's back with mother, for example

indicators.note: back means the word for father is read from right to left

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a mother is one example of a parent

explanation.surface: It is plain when Dad has returned home to Mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apparent is clearly visible or evident, readily seen by anyone.

clue.text: Carl's a spoilt rogue

indicators.note: spoilt suggests something damaged and put out of shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A judgement on Carl: an indulged child who has become a scamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Going rate for amphetamine?

blocks.note: first meaning: how fast something is travelling
second meaning: street slang for a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: Asking the current price of a stimulant drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Going rate looks like a market price, but it means rate of going.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means velocity of travel and is also common slang for the stimulant drug.

clue.text: Cause of food poisoning? It's the fish, girl!

blocks.note: a salmon is a fish
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Diagnosing a bout of sickness: the seafood the girl ate was off.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmonella bacteria infect contaminated eggs and meat and are a leading source of gastric illness.

clue.text: A sound return?

blocks.note: surface reading: a solid profit on an investment
setter's reading: sound is a noun, noise that bounces back off a surface

explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is noise reflected off a wall or cliff and heard again a moment later.

clue.text: Not even French is the most unusual

blocks.note: a number that is not even is odd
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: A remark that not even the French manage anything this strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of odd means strangest, the most peculiar of a group.

clue.text: Guide written by newspaper editor

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who shows the way
second meaning: the main opinion article in a paper

explanation.surface: A handbook penned by a press editor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the editorial column of a newspaper is called a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a person who heads others and the principal editorial piece in a British paper.
